_meta.note: This is the risk_register section of the .pmproj file. 15 risks covering all zones of the 5x5 matrix. 3 risks materialized as issues (R003, R009, R014). Residual scores use 1-5 scale. Load via File > Open > pmhelper_edu_reference.pmproj

risks.name: Lead Developer Extended Unavailability
risks.description: Omar Hassan El-Rashidy becomes unavailable for 4+ weeks due to illness, resignation, or competing opportunity. As the sole full-time technical resource, this directly threatens delivery of all development deliverables.
risks.response_description: Comprehensive code documentation maintained throughout. All architecture decisions captured in DECISIONS.md. GitHub commit history as knowledge base. AI-readable codebase (GitHub Copilot). Junior developer progressively cross-trained from Month 6 on core module structure.
risks.trigger_conditions: Omar reports health issues, has unplanned absences for >3 consecutive days, or raises employment concerns in 1-on-1.
risks.contingency_plan: Activate: (1) Junior Developer takes over routine tasks; (2) Sponsor approves emergency contractor hire (budget: EGP 5,000/day from management reserve); (3) Scope reduced to critical path only. Expected recovery: 3-4 week delay.

risks.name: Scope Creep from New PM Curriculum Requirements
risks.description: Faculty partners or the Sponsor request significant new features during Phases 3-6 (e.g., new calculation types, different UX paradigm, additional language support) that were not in the original scope.
risks.response_description: Formal change control process enforced. PM has authority to defer any new request requiring >2 days effort to V3 roadmap without sponsor escalation. All V1 and V2 features locked per EDU_V1_Plan.md and EDU_V2_Plan.md.
risks.trigger_conditions: More than 2 informal feature requests per sprint. Faculty beta tester suggests 'while you're at it' additions.
risks.contingency_plan: All requests logged in GitHub Issues with label 'v3-backlog'. PM presents consolidated backlog to Sponsor quarterly for prioritization. No new features approved without formal change request.

risks.name: PyInstaller Compatibility — Library Build Failures
risks.description: Known incompatibilities between PyInstaller's frozen import mechanism and scientific Python libraries (scipy, numpy, matplotlib) cause runtime errors in the compiled executable.
risks.response_description: Issue already MATERIALIZED (Issue I-001). Resolved with patch_scipy.py (wraps scipy.stats._distn_infrastructure.py NameError in try/except). Build pipeline (build_production.ps1) auto-applies patch at step 2b. Manifested in --onedir mode; --onefile approach rejected due to AV false positives.
risks.trigger_conditions: New library added to requirements.txt; Python version bump; PyInstaller version update.
risks.contingency_plan: Patch library maintained in patch_scipy.py. If new incompatibility emerges: (1) Add try/except around offending code; (2) Test with PyInstaller --collect-all flag; (3) Worst case: pin PyInstaller to last known-good version.

risks.name: GitHub Copilot Unavailability or Price Increase
risks.description: GitHub Copilot subscription is cancelled, pricing increases beyond budget, or service is discontinued. The project budget assumes EGP 950/month for Copilot, representing approximately 30-40% of development velocity.
risks.response_description: Alternative AI tools documented and ready: Claude.ai (Anthropic), GPT-4 Turbo (OpenAI), Cursor IDE. Codebase is well-documented enough to continue with reduced AI assistance. Budget includes 20% buffer for subscription cost increases.
risks.trigger_conditions: GitHub email about pricing changes; Copilot subscription renewal notification; service degradation > 3 days.
risks.contingency_plan: Switch to Cursor IDE + Claude.ai (combined cost similar to Copilot). Adjust development velocity estimates: -15% expected impact with alternative tools.

risks.name: Render.com Infrastructure Pricing or Service Change
risks.description: Render.com increases free/starter tier limitations (memory, CPU, sleep behavior) or changes pricing in ways that make the current deployment uneconomical or non-functional.
risks.response_description: Fallback deployment options fully documented: Railway.app (similar pricing), Fly.io (better performance on free tier), Heroku Eco Dynos. Docker configuration (Dockerfile, docker-compose.yml) enables rapid migration. Application stateless design allows provider switch in < 4 hours.
risks.trigger_conditions: Render.com pricing announcement; application response time > 5 seconds consistently; sleep/cold-start behavior impacting demo quality.
risks.contingency_plan: Execute provider migration script. Update render.yaml equivalent (railway.toml or fly.toml). Update documentation. Expected migration time: 4 hours.

risks.name: Python Version Incompatibility in University Labs
risks.description: Some Egyptian university computer labs run Python 3.6 or 3.7 (outdated) due to IT policies. The application requires Python 3.8+. The Windows exe mitigates this for most users but source-code users are affected.
risks.response_description: PyInstaller exe (D3) bundles Python 3.11 — completely immune to lab Python version. PyPI installation automatically enforces Python 3.8+ requirement. Faculty documentation includes clear system requirements. Testing on Python 3.8 as minimum (CI/CD enforced).
risks.trigger_conditions: Faculty partner reports installation failure on lab machines.
risks.contingency_plan: Direct faculty to exe distribution for lab use. Provide IT department with system requirements documentation (PMHE-2025-IT-001).

risks.name: WebView2 Not Available in Lab Environments
risks.description: The Plotly interactive charts (S-Curve, Gantt, Network) use WebView2 (Chromium-based) embedded in the desktop app. Some Windows lab builds lack WebView2 or block its installation.
risks.response_description: Issue PARTIALLY MATERIALIZED (Issue I-003). Graceful fallback implemented: PlotlyChartFrame checks WebView2 availability at startup; if unavailable, defaults to Matplotlib rendering. Educational value is preserved. All interactive features degrade gracefully to static charts.
risks.trigger_conditions: Application startup on a machine without Edge/WebView2 installed.
risks.contingency_plan: No action needed — graceful fallback already implemented. Optional: include WebView2 bootstrapper in GitHub Release package.

risks.name: EVM Formula Misalignment with PMBOK Revision
risks.description: PMI releases a revised PMBOK 7th Edition supplement or CAPM/PMP exam content outline change that uses different EVM formulas or terminology, making the current application inconsistent with exam preparation.
risks.response_description: Prof. Youssef Ibrahim Tawfik (Technical Advisor) monitors PMI curriculum changes as part of his advisory role. Monthly content review sessions catch changes. PMBOK 6th Edition is the verified baseline for V1 + V2. Formula code is in evm_calculations_edu.py (pure functions — easy to update).
risks.trigger_conditions: PMI curriculum announcement; CAPM/PMP exam content outline revision published.
risks.contingency_plan: Update evm_calculations_edu.py and evm_tab_edu.py with revised formulas. Update educational annotations. Release as patch version (e.g., v1.1.1).

risks.name: Systematic Project Duration Underestimate
risks.description: The project consistently takes longer than estimated per deliverable due to the inherent complexity of educational software (worked solutions, dual-mode UG/PG, interactive visualisations). This compounds over the project lifecycle.
risks.response_description: MATERIALIZED (Issue I-002). CPI at Month 10 = 0.92. The project has incurred approximately EGP 80,000 more than estimated. Root cause: educational scaffolding (worked solutions, Try It Yourself mode) required more development time than budgeted. Contingency reserve (EGP 122,652) is sufficient to absorb. Management reserve not required.
risks.trigger_conditions: CPI < 0.95 for two consecutive months (TRIGGER POINT WAS MISSED AT MONTH 4).
risks.contingency_plan: Contingency reserve utilisation: ~EGP 80,000 of EGP 122,652 available = 65% used. Remaining reserve EGP 42,652 covers final 3 months. If reserve exhausted, request management reserve release from Sponsor.

risks.name: Institutional Adoption Lower Than Projected
risks.description: Universities and training centres adopt PMHelper_Edu at a slower rate than projected in the Business Case (target: 3 institutions by Year 1, 8 by Year 2), reducing revenue and NPV.
risks.response_description: Business risk — mitigated by: (1) free open-source model removes cost barrier; (2) faculty beta testing program creates advocates before launch; (3) reference sample project reduces faculty effort to adopt; (4) Prof. Youssef's network provides access to first adopter institutions.
risks.trigger_conditions: < 1 institutional adoption by Month 3 post-launch; < 50 GitHub stars by Month 6 post-launch.
risks.contingency_plan: Activate marketing plan: conference presentation, academic LinkedIn campaign, direct email to 30 target faculty. Revisit Business Case NPV assumptions at 12-month post-launch review.

risks.name: Angular Framework Major Version Incompatibility
risks.description: Angular releases a major version with breaking changes (e.g., Angular 19 to 20) that requires significant web frontend rework before the production release deadline.
risks.response_description: Pin Angular version in package.json. Use LTS (Long Term Support) releases only. Version specified in requirements documentation. Migration guide reviewed before any version upgrade.
risks.trigger_conditions: Angular announces major version with breaking changes in API used by the application.
risks.contingency_plan: Defer Angular version upgrade to V3. Maintain current LTS version for V1 + V2 release cycle.

risks.name: PyPI Package Name Conflict
risks.description: The package name 'pmhelper' on PyPI is taken by another project, blocking D4 acceptance (pip install pmhelper must work).
risks.response_description: RESOLVED. Package name 'pmhelper' confirmed available on PyPI and already registered. pyproject.toml configured with correct metadata. Package name conflict risk is now CLOSED.
risks.trigger_conditions: PyPI submission rejection citing name conflict.
risks.contingency_plan: Alternative names prepared: pmhelper-edu, pmhelper-pm, pmproject-edu. Legal review not required (MIT license open-source).

risks.name: Educational Content Misalignment with PMBOK
risks.description: Worked solutions, formulas, or terminology in the application contradict PMBOK 6th Edition standards, discovered during UAT or post-launch, damaging academic credibility.
risks.response_description: Monthly content review sessions with Prof. Youssef (Technical Advisor). All EVM formulas verified against PMBOK 6th Edition Appendix X3. Faculty beta testing includes educational accuracy verification. Annotated educational versions explicitly reference PMBOK process numbers.
risks.trigger_conditions: Faculty partner flags formula discrepancy during beta test; CAPM/PMP candidate reports exam inconsistency.
risks.contingency_plan: Immediate patch release with corrected formula. Update all annotation documents. Prof. Youssef posts clarification on product GitHub if warranted.

risks.name: CI/CD Pipeline Intermittent Failures
risks.description: GitHub Actions workflow produces false positive test failures due to timing issues (Monte Carlo randomness), environment differences, or GitHub Actions resource limits, blocking merges.
risks.response_description: PARTIALLY MATERIALIZED (Issue I-004 minor). Monte Carlo tests seed-pinned (seed=42) for reproducibility. Test isolation enforced. Maximum retry added for flaky tests. GitHub Actions status monitored via badge on README.
risks.trigger_conditions: CI badge shows red on main branch for >24 hours without code change.
risks.contingency_plan: Re-run CI pipeline (GitHub Actions UI). If persistent: isolate failing test, add seed pin, or mark as skip-ci for urgent hot fixes.

risks.name: University Lab Internet Restrictions Block Web Version
risks.description: Some university IT policies block external websites or restrict browser access in lab environments, preventing students from accessing the web application even if the desktop version is available.
risks.response_description: Desktop exe (D3) is the primary distribution for lab environments — fully offline, no internet required. Web application is a supplementary channel for personal devices and home use. IT restriction impact is limited to the web channel only.
risks.trigger_conditions: Faculty partner reports browser blocking during beta test in lab environment.
risks.contingency_plan: Document for IT departments: 'For restricted lab environments, use the Windows executable (no internet required). The web application is optional and complementary.'
